knownFailures.list-ends: Llama 3 can invent a scan when eviction reads the last list entry directly. A correct answer is an improvement, not a failure.

cases.question: In BuzzDB v015's LRU buffer manager, which end of lruList holds the most recently used page, and which end supplies the eviction victim?
cases.idealAnswer: The front holds the most recently used page. The back holds the least recently used page and supplies the eviction victim.

requiredFacts.requirement: The most recently used page is at the front.
requiredFacts.referenceQuote: The front holds the most recently used page.

requiredFacts.requirement: The least recently used page at the back is the eviction victim.
requiredFacts.referenceQuote: The back holds the least recently used page and supplies the eviction victim.

cases.question: What happens to an already cached page when I access it again?
cases.idealAnswer: The accessed page moves to the front, becoming the most recently used page. A cache hit does not require loading that page from disk.

requiredFacts.requirement: Accessing a cached page moves it to the front and makes it most recently used.
requiredFacts.referenceQuote: The accessed page moves to the front, becoming the most recently used page.

cases.question: Why does that help keep frequently used pages in memory?
cases.idealAnswer: Each repeated access renews the page at the most recently used end. Untouched pages become older and are evicted first. This favors temporal locality, although scans can undermine LRU.

requiredFacts.requirement: Repeated access refreshes recency, so untouched older pages are evicted first.
requiredFacts.referenceQuote: Each repeated access renews the page at the most recently used end. Untouched pages become older and are evicted first.
